counterevidence: Current README text is a CURRENT_SNAPSHOT and cannot explain historical star growth.
Several successful CLIs document more than one installer when those installers agree. The claim is about a contradiction, not about deleting every extra installer.
Star movement is underpowered for a repository with fewer than 30 stars, so stars are not the success metric.
Platform-owned repositories are excluded from the supporting set.

One-command install is already present on dalance/amber, lmnr-ai/index, neovateai/neovate-code, shotgun-sh/shotgun, and those controls are not in the same star regime as their matched breakouts. This is not a causal claim.
hypothesis.text: Making contradictory install instructions agree may reduce activation friction. This is not a causal claim.

sections.fact: README fields in this study are a CURRENT_SNAPSHOT pinned by blob SHA. They were not observed before the growth window, so they cannot explain historical stars.
sections.hypothesis: A file-level install contradiction is a reversible trial. It does not establish a cause of stars.
sections.interpretation: The casebook is a retrospective selection. Comparative star claims stay UNKNOWN.

claims.text: README fields in this study are a CURRENT_SNAPSHOT pinned by blob SHA. They were not observed before the growth window, so they cannot explain historical stars.

transferability.why_might: The supporting cases include a low-brand maintainer, and the change is a file the target maintainer can edit.
transferability.why_might_not: A low-brand case still does not show that the same change caused adoption. Audience, age, and launch channel can differ. The band is not an effect size. It does not match on age, and a current README cannot explain historical stars.
